name: A Chart of the Pacific Ocean from the Equinoctial to the Latitude of 39½d. No., engraved by R. W. Seale, Plate XLI in Richard Walter, A Voyage Round the World ... by George Anson (London, 1748)
holding: Royal Museums Greenwich, F0126 (uncoloured, the whole plate, 7695 x 2399)
licence: public domain (1748); RMG scan, public domain on Commons
note: The Spanish galleon chart Anson took from the Nuestra Señora de Covadonga in June 1743, re-engraved for Walter's account of the voyage. It is how the Manila galleons' own chart of the North Pacific reached English and French cartography, and it draws 'Donna Maria Lazara' as a small island with a drawn coast — a crooked boot, toe to the west, a hook to the east — about 35 x 28 px on this scan. No other depiction with a coastline was found: Stieler 1826 (the story's plate) names it with no island, and Arrowsmith 1798 has already dropped it. Etienne picked this plate over the hand-coloured Geographicus copy (Commons, 'Pacific-anson-1748', the right half only, 5000 px): the colourist's green wash there does not follow the engraved coast — it cuts the toe short, rounds the hook off and runs over the coast on the west — and the JPEG has blurred the engraved line under it into a broken one. Both are prints of the same copper plate, so the engraver's line is the shape, and it is crisp only here.
projection_note: MERCATOR (a 'reduced' chart), not a plate carree. The latitude scale along the plate's central meridian spaces its degrees about 53 px apart near the equator and about 70 px near 38 N, a ratio of 1.32 against sec 38 = 1.27; and on the coloured copy Guadalupe falls at 29.4 N read as Mercator (equator at the scale bar's upper rule) against a real 29.0 N, where a plate carree would put it at 30.8 N. Longitude is counted east from San Bernardino, so it is not used.
scale_note: Size only, from the sheet's own degree, read at the island's latitude on the chart. The sheet oversizes islands, as atlas sheets do: Guadalupe is drawn ~60 x 65 km at this scale against a real ~35 x 10 km. The sheet's scale is kept anyway, as it was for Saint-Mathieu on Ortelius' Africa.
extraction_note: --mode dark --threshold 145 (grey < 110) --strip 3 --closing 2. There is no wash on this copy, the coast is one engraved line, and two rhumb lines as thin as that line cross the island. --open would erase the coast with them; --mode ink floods from inside but stops at every hatched part of the interior, and lost the head and the toe (24 x 22 px against 35 x 28). --strip, added for this island, fills holes first — the outline becomes solid, the rhumb lines stay lines — and then opens them away. Plateau: grey 110-120 at strip 3 gives 469-471 px, 35 x 28. The edge sits on the engraved line.
scale_measured: 53.15 px per degree of longitude, fitted on 122 half-degree ticks of the equator scale across x 3114-7494 (rms 1.9 px); equator at y 2296, the scale bar's upper rule. The island's centre (y ~806) is 28.05 Mercator degrees above it, i.e. 27.0 N on the chart, where one px is 111.32 cos 27.0 / 53.15 = 1.866 km.
